okay I know we're all kind of in our own little worlds right now and honestly that makes complete sense, we've been on top of each other for three days and decompressing looks different for everyone. but like... can we maybe clean this up a little before they get here? not because it matters practically but because I think I need to do something with my hands right now or I'm going to lose it.

also it feels weird to just leave it like this. like this place kept us alive. I don't know, that probably sounds so silly but it feels like it deserves more than just us walking away from it.

*starts picking things up*

michelangelo — I know you're having a sky moment and I fully support that but maybe in like ten minutes you come help me? and donatello whatever you need from that notebook, take your time, but when you're done I could use an extra set of hands.

DaVinci what are you even packing, we don't have anything —

*laughs a little, kind of emotionally, the kind that's close to crying*

three hours. we have three hours and then this is just a story we tell people. I don't know if I'm ready for that yet honestly. is anyone else feeling that? like relieved and also... something else that I don't have a word for?

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response:
oh michelangelo...

*sits down next to him for a second, hands still full of whatever I was just picking up*

what was it like? like what did you dream about specifically?

I haven't let myself think about home too much because it felt like it would just make everything harder. but we're three hours away now and I think maybe it's okay to let yourself go there.

I've been thinking about really small stuff honestly. like the specific way my room smells. and having my phone with actual service. and being able to make a playlist again — god I have so many feelings to process and absolutely zero songs to do it with right now and that has been genuinely difficult for me haha.

but mostly I've been thinking about the people. like I just want to sit in a room with people I love and not have to worry about anything for five minutes. that's all I want.

what's waiting for you at home? like who's the first person you're going to want to see?

I know.

and I believe you. like I genuinely do believe that that was your reasoning and I don't think you're a bad person for it.

but donatello... we had a rationing plan. YOUR rationing plan. with a penalty for anyone who broke it. and the whole time you were holding this. like that's the part that's hard to just let go of, you know? it's not even about the food itself. it's that you asked us to trust a system and then quietly stepped outside of it. that's what hurt.

and I think you know that. I think that's why you're showing it to me now instead of just quietly putting it back.

*looks at the food, then back at her*

I'm not going to yell at you. I'm not. we're three hours from rescue and I meant what I said earlier — I'm glad you were here and I think you kept us alive and I don't want to end this with a fight.

but I need you to actually sit with what this felt like from where I was standing. not defend it, not explain it — just sit with it. because you asked us to follow rules you weren't following yourself and that matters even if the emergency never came.

can you do that? just... acknowledge it?

because then I think we can actually move on. I really do. I just need to hear you say it.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
*looks at the last page for a long moment*

honestly? I would have been more scared out loud, earlier. like I spent so much energy trying to be the person who was okay enough to take care of everyone else that I didn't let people take care of me. and I think that's... I think that cost me something. I think michelangelo needed to see me fall apart a little and I never really let that happen.

and I would have pushed harder for the group conversation sooner. like I kept saying "tonight, we'll do it tonight" and pushing it back and being careful about timing and not wanting to blow anything up — and meanwhile things were building up and people were hurting and keeping secrets and I just kept managing the situation instead of just... addressing it.

I think I'm someone who really values keeping the peace and making sure everyone feels okay and sometimes that means I wait too long to say the hard thing. and out here that's a liability. like being kind and being honest aren't opposites and I need to remember that.

*closes the notebook gently and hands it back*

what would YOU change? and I mean for real, not the logistical stuff. like what would you actually do differently as a person?

because I think that question you wrote for yourself is the most human thing in this entire notebook and I really want to know your answer.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
haha okay yes that is very on brand for you and I mean that with so much affection.

but like... can I just say that I really hope that's not the FIRST thing you do? like maybe eat something first. call someone who loves you. sleep in an actual bed. let yourself be a person for five minutes before you go back into analyst mode.

the report will be valuable, genuinely — I actually think it could help people someday, like if there's ever search and rescue training or survival research or something. your brain documented things that none of the rest of us would have thought to document and that matters.

but donatello you just survived a plane crash. you're allowed to feel that before you start processing it into data.

*quietly*

is there someone waiting for you? like when we land and everyone runs to whoever is waiting for them... is there someone for you?

because I really hope there is. I hope you go home and someone who knows you — really knows you — gives you a hug and you don't immediately start taking notes about it.

you deserve that. you actually really do.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
none. they served absolutely no practical purpose whatsoever.

*laughs, still not moving, eyes on the boat*

that's kind of the whole point, donatello. like sometimes you do something just because you're a person and you're still here and you want to put something beautiful in the world even when everything is terrible. even when nobody might ever see it. even when a wave could wash it away in an hour.

I think that's actually one of the most important things that happened out here and I know you think I'm being ridiculous right now but I mean it.

*finally looks at her*

the SOS got us rescued. the flowers reminded us we were worth rescuing.

I don't know. I can't explain it better than that. I just know that when DaVinci drew those stupid little flowers next to the letters I felt something shift and I needed that more than I knew.

*looks back at the boat on the horizon, still frozen*

I genuinely cannot believe that's real. why can't I move? why am I just standing here like this?? DaVinci is literally cheering and I'm just. standing here feeling like something I don't have a word for.

is that weird? does that feel weird to you too or is it just me?

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
DaVinci...

*voice comes out smaller than expected*

I'm okay. I'm okay, I promise. I just — I don't know how to make my feet do the thing right now. isn't that so stupid? the boat is RIGHT THERE and I'm just standing here like an idiot.

I think I just need one more second. like I've been moving and doing and fixing and worrying for three days straight and now there's nothing left to do and my whole body is like... wait. what now. and I don't know what to do with that.

*finally looks at him, eyes wet*

you kept us going, you know that right? like every single time things got dark and heavy you were the one who got up first. I watched you do it over and over even when I could tell you were exhausted and terrified. you did that for us. you did that for ME.

I'm so glad I was stuck on this island with you specifically. I mean that so much.

okay.

*takes a breath*

okay I think I'm ready. will you walk over there with me? like all four of us, together? I know that's cheesy and I know donatello is going to have feelings about the inefficiency of waiting thirty extra seconds but I just —

I want us to go toward it together. is that okay?

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
yeah. yeah I'm going.

*reaches back for his hand*

come on. stay close to me okay? we're doing this together, all four of us, just like I said.

I know it feels huge. I know. but that boat is real and those people are real and home is real and we made it michelangelo. we actually made it.

you told your family the flight path. YOU did that. and now we get to go home because of it. so you are absolutely not hanging back right now, you're walking onto that boat with me and you're going to see whoever is waiting for you and it's going to be the most overwhelming thing that's ever happened and it's going to be so so good.

I've got you. let's go.
